newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN says 13 Iraqi oil sales contracts now approved.
newsitem.headline: UN says 13 Iraqi oil sales contracts now approved.

text.p: The United Nations said Wednesday evening that it has now approved 13 contracts under the "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq, up from 10 earlier in the day.
U.N. spokesman Juan-Carlos Brandt said there are currently no contracts awaiting approval by the U.N.'s overseers.

The U.N. has been approving contracts fairly speedily under the terms of the deal, which allows Baghdad to export up to $2 billion of oil over six months, on a renewable basis, to pay for badly needed food, medicines and other humanitarian goods.
Baghdad said in the last few days under the terms of the deal, which was given the green light by the U.N. on December 9, it has signed agreements with 20 oil companies, up from 11 last week.

The first Iraqi oil exports for six years left from the Gulf port of Mina al-bakr earlier Wednesday. The supertanker Star Africa, chartered by U.S. oil firm Coastal Corp, left port with the first oil under the company's 60,000 barrels per day contract.
